research_question: Can the global constant–clock framework of arXiv:2502.00081 be connected to the existing autonomous lattice clock to obtain testable laws for dimensionless constants?

external_source.title: How to make a Universe
external_source.read_scope: HTML main text sections I–IX; detailed algebra focus II–V. No inference of human reading.

claims.claim: The source supplies a conditional global canonical architecture and does not uniquely select the inverse-log-square response.
A monotone response can be used as a canonical coordinate; the existing clock kinetic term must be retained, so the connection is an extension rather than an exact identification of the source model.
A positive gauge kinetic response can connect the clock to alpha, with specified physical couplings, time calibration and feedback assumptions.
A single common linear response gives rank-one normalized variations and a precise, nonconstant-in-general logarithmic drift ratio.
The bridge does not establish matter creation, a Riemann origin of physical interactions, the observed variation of constants, or a unique exponent p=2.

negative_constraints: Do not identify the source generic alpha with electromagnetic alpha.
Do not identify canonical clocks, R, model time and cosmic age without an explicit map.
Do not delete clock kinetic energy or backreaction.
Do not promote a chosen B(R) into a derivation of electromagnetic coupling from Riemann zeros.
Do not carry the old tail theorem into a newly coupled electromagnetic model without new conditions.

review_scope: One native shared-context subagent checked canonical algebra and physical interface assumptions; not external peer review.
